title: Tension Envelope: Stalled CRM project done | enCloud9
meta: How enCloud9 restarted Tension Envelope's stalled Dynamics 365 Sales project, integrating its data warehouse and training an in-house SME within three months.
h1: A stalled CRM project brought to life
answer: Tension Envelope in Kansas City, MO is the second largest envelope producer in the United States. Its Dynamics 365 Sales project had stalled after trouble with a prior deployment partner. We integrated the system with its data warehouse, completed Sales Hub updates and trained an internal subject matter expert. The dormant project came to life within three months.
tiles: to bring a dormant project to life
outcomes: A project that had been dormant for some time was brought to life within three months.
Integration with Tension's data warehouse streamlined management of client orders and budgets.
An internal subject matter expert can now handle user queries, make minor customizations and pass knowledge to other team members.
enCloud9 offers continuous support and consultation.
chapters: What was wrong with Tension's CRM?

Tension is a privately held company that designs and manufactures billions of envelopes each year for clients in billing, finance and direct marketing. It is the second largest envelope producer in the United States.
Its Dynamics 365 Sales project had stagnated after problems with its prior Dynamics 365 deployment partner. A recommendation from its data analytics partner led it to enCloud9.
We integrated the system with Tension's data warehouse to streamline management of client orders and budgets, and completed updates to the Sales Hub.
We also trained a subject matter expert inside Tension to handle user queries, make minor customizations and share knowledge with other team members.

Tension manages client orders and budgets through the integrated system, and its own subject matter expert handles user questions and minor changes, with enCloud9 providing continuous support and consultation.
author: Kristin Caniglia
